provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Event family batch. Mostly a rebuild sale. The demo uses marked placeholders, never their portfolio, until written permission. No marketplaces or gallery-delivery brands named. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.section: How many hours of wedding coverage
pageStructurePlus.contains: Getting ready, first look, ceremony, family formals, golden hour portraits and the send-off laid out on a sample wedding day timeline, with what each extra hour of coverage adds
pageStructurePlus.why: Couples don't know how many hours to buy and compare photographers on hours alone. A timeline shows why the right package costs what it does.

pageStructurePlus.contains: A form for family groupings, VIP names, notes on divorced or late parents, who wrangles the groups, and how long formals take
pageStructurePlus.why: Family formals are where wedding days run late and feelings get hurt. A photographer who plans them ahead looks like the safe choice to the parents.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Engagement locations around the area, outfit advice, best light times of year, session length and whether the engagement shoot is included
pageStructurePlus.why: The engagement session is often the first booking and the couple's first real experience of the photographer. A guide makes it feel planned.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Courthouse, trail and park elopements, [permit] notes, short coverage blocks, travel fees and an elopement planning checklist
pageStructurePlus.why: Elopement couples search separately and want short coverage with real planning help. A page for them catches bookings a full-day package scares off.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Sneak peek timing, full gallery delivery in weeks, print release, heirloom album spreads, parent albums and wall art options
pageStructurePlus.why: Couples ask 'when do we get them' before they ask about style. Clear delivery times and album options raise the average package.

designDirections.name: Date Check First
designDirections.bestFor: Newer wedding photographers who need booked enquiries more than a gallery-led brand
designDirections.headlineSample: Wedding photographer in {City}. Is your date open?
designDirections.whyItFits: The family combo, used where conversion matters most. Bold poster type and a strong accent keep the date check above one signature frame.

designDirections.name: White Gallery
designDirections.bestFor: Established wedding photographers whose galleries do the selling and who book by venue and season
designDirections.whyItFits: Not the family combo: the ultramarine accent fights wedding colour. A white gallery with a Didone display steps back and lets the work lead.

designDirections.name: Noir Editorial
designDirections.bestFor: Luxury and editorial wedding photographers taking a limited number of weddings a year
designDirections.whyItFits: A dark editorial page makes every frame the brightest thing on screen, and the type-led hero signals a waitlist, not a discount.

openers.angle: Bio link to a client gallery
openers.line: Your bio link goes to a client proofing gallery rather than a wedding photographer's site, so an engaged couple can see one wedding but not your packages, coverage hours or whether you're free on their date.
openers.hook: Tap their bio link and note where it lands: a proofing gallery, a link page or a PDF.
openers.linkLine: Your wedding work with packages and a date check: {demo-link}

openers.line: I could only find your wedding photography on a Facebook page, where the newest weddings bury the best ones. Couples planning a year out want to see full weddings in one place before they enquire.
openers.hook: Search their business name and confirm the Facebook page is the only real presence. Note when the last album went up.
openers.linkLine: Your wedding photography as a site couples can browse: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your photography site still runs an old template with a contact form that doesn't ask for the wedding date. So every enquiry starts with checking whether the day is even free.
openers.hook: Open the contact form and check for a wedding date field. Note any other dated detail like an old year in the footer.
openers.linkLine: The same photographer, with the wedding date asked first: {demo-link}

openers.line: I opened your wedding gallery on my phone and waited a long time for the first frame. Couples browse photographers in bed on their phones and move on fast.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load the main gallery on your phone and time it. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: A wedding gallery built to load fast on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: There's no starting price for wedding coverage anywhere on your site. Couples with a set photography budget often skip the photographer who makes them ask.
openers.hook: Check the site, the bio and any pricing guide for a 'from' figure. If there is none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A wedding photography page with honest starting prices: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your best weddings sit in one long portfolio grid with no venue names. A couple getting married at that same venue wants to see the full day there, not a single frame.
openers.hook: Find a recent wedding they posted and note the venue name. Mention it if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your weddings, organised by venue and season: {demo-link}

openers.line: One of your Google reviews says you kept grandma calm through the family formals. That's the sentence a nervous bride's mother needs to read on the wedding photographer's own site.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase about the day, the formals or the gallery. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your couple reviews beside the weddings they describe: {demo-link}

openers.line: December proposals mean January enquiries. Wedding photographers with a date check and a pricing guide ready by then catch the couples who book their photographer right after the venue.
openers.hook: Use this from October to January. Check whether they've posted about booking next year.
openers.linkLine: A wedding photography site ready for engagement season: {demo-link}

openers.line: Couples send wedding photographer enquiries late at night after planning sessions. If the reply waits until you're done editing next afternoon, they may have booked a call with someone else.
openers.hook: Look for comments like 'are you available' or 'what are your rates'. Note one with its time.
openers.linkLine: A wedding photography enquiry that replies with your pricing guide straight away: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're looking for a second shooter for next season. Good wedding photographers check how established you look online before they commit their Saturdays.
openers.hook: Only if they posted for a second shooter or associate. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: A wedding photography site with an associate team page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Couples who booked a venue search the venue's name plus 'photographer'. You've shot weddings at a few well-known venues, and none of them have a page on your site.
openers.hook: List two or three venues they've tagged in wedding posts. Name one if they reply.
openers.linkLine: A page for each venue you've photographed weddings at: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your wedding photography packages don't mention a retainer or payment schedule anywhere I could find. A clear retainer and payment schedule makes a bigger package easier to say yes to.
openers.hook: Look for 'retainer', 'payment plan' or 'deposit' in their pricing info. Note what they publish and never invent terms.
openers.linkLine: A wedding package page with the retainer and payment schedule explained: {demo-link}

openers.line: Venues often ask wedding photographers for proof of insurance before the day. A short line on the site saying you provide it makes planners comfortable recommending you.
openers.hook: Check whether they mention insurance or venue requirements. Never state coverage or credentials they haven't published.
openers.linkLine: A wedding photographer site with the venue paperwork answered: {demo-link}

openers.line: It looks like a lot of your weddings come from venue preferred lists. When a venue changes its list, the couples it used to send you need to find you on your own.
openers.hook: Look for posts thanking a venue or a planner for referrals. Name the relationship if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Where an engaged couple would find you without the venue list: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you shared is lovely wedding work. A full gallery from a day like that should be the first thing an engaged couple sees, with the venue named.
openers.hook: Pick their newest posted wedding and name it exactly: the venue, the season and the moment they featured.
openers.linkLine: That wedding, as a full story on your site: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner} — that {specific recent job} you shared is lovely wedding work.

I looked at the site for {Business Name} and couldn't find a starting price or a way to check a wedding date. I put together a sample photographer site with packages, coverage hours and a date check, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. I don't use anyone's work without written permission.

Would you like me to send it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner} — following up in case my message got lost between edits. Here's the sample wedding photography site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has a date check, starting prices, a coverage-hours timeline and a family formals form. The galleries are marked placeholders until you say which weddings to use. If it's not for you, say so and I won't message again.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for wedding photographers around {City}. I sent you a message a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"Easy to miss in editing season. Short version: I built a sample wedding photography site for {Business Name} with a date check, packages and a coverage timeline. The galleries are marked placeholders where your photos would go, nothing of yours is on it. Can I email you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
 → ask: "How many enquiries a month are for dates you've already booked?"
"The rebuild runs {Build Range}, then {Care Range} a month for hosting, new galleries and price changes. For a wedding photographer at your level I'd normally quote about {Build Price}."
"Can we walk through it for fifteen minutes on a weekday, away from a wedding weekend?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. You pick the weddings for the galleries and confirm in writing that I can use them."

objections.handler: "You do, and the work on it is good. The gap is the date check and the starting price. Couples who can't tell if you're free or in budget enquire with someone who tells them."

objections.objection: All my couples find me on Instagram.
objections.handler: "Instagram finds them. Before they book, they look for packages, coverage hours and full weddings. The site answers that and sends them back to your grid if they want more."
"Then the site is for raising your prices and choosing your weddings. A date check and a pricing guide let the right couples find you a year earlier."

objections.objection: I don't want my work used without permission.
objections.handler: "Agreed, and it isn't. The demo has marked placeholders where your photos would go. Nothing of yours goes on until you choose the weddings and confirm in writing."

objections.objection: I get my couples from wedding listing sites.
objections.handler: "Keep those. Couples who find you there still open your own site before they enquire. That's where the starting price and the date check close it."

objections.objection: I'm in editing season, I have no time.
objections.handler: "You don't need any. I build it from your public info and the weddings you pick, then you approve it once. It's live before engagement season starts."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, because it's a date check, packages and galleries by venue. One wedding booking covers it."

email.subject: Wedding photography site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "Hi {Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for wedding photographers in {City}, and I put together a sample for {Business Name} with a date check and starting prices. I'll email you the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner} — I'm taking the {Business Name} wedding photography demo down on Friday to free up the space.

Want me to leave it up? One word is fine either way.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner} — proposal season is close, and couples start booking photographers in January, right after the venue. Thought of you.

The sample site is still here, still with marked placeholders, and nothing's changed on price. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Price the rebuild against one wedding booking. Most already have a site, so you are selling enquiries that convert, not a first site.
Price galleries by wedding story, not page count. Each venue gallery needs a write-up, vendor credits and the couple's OK.
The date check and pricing guide are the core of the rebuild. Never let them become optional.
Venue pages are their own line. They are what ranks for the venue name plus photographer.
Keep monthly add-ons under the cost of one engagement session.
Sell anything for engagement season by October, before the editing backlog takes over.

lineItems.description: Max with a written story of the day, vendor credits, the venue named and a permission record from the couple.

lineItems.item: Venue page for a photographed venue
lineItems.description: Max with several weddings at that venue, best light notes, and the ceremony and portrait spots on the grounds.

lineItems.item: Pricing guide behind a date and email form
lineItems.description: Max with a designed multi-page guide, collections, album options and an automatic reply that sends it.
Max when couples enter ceremony time and sunset and see the suggested coverage block.
Max with groupings by side, VIP names, sensitive family notes and a printable list for the day.

lineItems.item: Album and wall art proof page
lineItems.description: Max with album spreads, parent albums and wall art options the couple can choose from.
Max with several locations, [permit] placeholders, a planning checklist and short coverage blocks.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile upkeep for the photography studio
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A recent wedding on your Google profile every week with the venue named, so couples searching for a wedding photographer near that venue find you first."

whatElseYouSell.name: Review requests after gallery delivery
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "The day after the couple opens their wedding gallery, they get a short note asking for a review while they're still crying over the first look."

whatElseYouSell.name: Venue-name search pages for weddings
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Each month a new page for a venue you've photographed weddings at, so couples searching that venue name plus photographer land on you."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, once they list the venues they've shot and which couples gave permission.

whatElseYouSell.name: Engagement season enquiry push
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A January push to newly engaged couples with the pricing guide and open dates, timed for the weeks they book their wedding photographer."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in October, run between Christmas and March.

whatElseYouSell.name: Bridal show booth kit for the photographer
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Print panels from your chosen weddings, a date-check card and a sign-up code, so couples at the bridal show leave as enquiries, not brochures."
whatElseYouSell.when: Six weeks before their first winter bridal show.

whatElseYouSell.name: Preferred-list pitch packet for wedding venues
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A short packet for venue coordinators with weddings you've shot at their venue, your insurance line and how you work with their timeline."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, before venues refresh their vendor lists for next season.

whatElseYouSell.name: Styled shoot coordination with local vendors
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "I line up the venue, florist and hair and makeup for a styled wedding shoot and handle the credits, so you just show up and photograph it."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 4, in the off-season, when they want new work in a style they're not booked for yet.

whatElseYouSell.name: Real wedding blog publishing
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Two real weddings a month written up with the venue, vendors and the couple's story, published on your photography site."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, if they say writing blog posts is the part they never get to.

withoutAI.route: Small venues the photographer shoots often
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The barn where you photograph a wedding every month still has no site of its own. You can introduce me at your next wedding there."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Photographers know which venues are under-served and the owners trust them. Your client's galleries can even fill the venue site, with permission.

withoutAI.route: Hair and makeup artists on the same weddings
withoutAI.whoPays: The artist, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The bridal hair and makeup team in every getting-ready shot books trials by DM. A small date-check site fits them, and the photographer can make the intro."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Getting-ready vendors share the morning with the photographer. A referral from the person who made them look good lands well.

withoutAI.route: Florists credited in the wedding galleries
withoutAI.whoPays: The florist, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The florist you credit in so many of your weddings has no wedding portfolio online. The photographer's own shots of their work make the case."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Florists need beautiful pictures and photographers have them. The introduction comes with proof attached.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The bridal boutique your brides keep naming needs a fitting appointment page and a real-brides gallery. Your client photographs those dresses every weekend."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Boutiques want real weddings in their dresses. Photographers have them and are trusted for them.

withoutAI.route: Videographers who pair with the photographer
withoutAI.whoPays: The videographer, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The videographer you share weddings with is still Instagram-only. Same date-check layout, built for wedding films."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Photo and video teams book together and refer constantly. One finished site sells the second.

withoutAI.route: Local frame shops that print their wall art
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The frame shop that prints your wedding wall art has no way for couples to order online. I'll build an ordering page they can share with every photographer."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Frame shops depend on photographer referrals and rarely have a modern site.

withAI.route: Fitting appointment assistant for bridal boutiques
withAI.pitchLine: "Brides ask the boutique about styles, budgets and fitting slots any hour, and get an appointment without waiting for a callback."
withAI.whyItWorks: Boutiques lose appointments after hours. The photographer's introduction gets you a meeting.

withAI.route: Bridal trial booking assistant for makeup artists
withAI.pitchLine: "The bride's party size, wedding date and venue go in, and the makeup artist gets a quote draft and a trial slot to confirm."
withAI.whyItWorks: Bridal hair and makeup quoting is repetitive and done between appointments. It's small and easy to say yes to.

withAI.pitchLine: "From the photographer's gallery credits and the couple's details, the venue gets a real-wedding feature draft to publish with permission."
withAI.whyItWorks: Venues want real weddings on their site and never get them written. The photographer supplies the source.

withAI.pitchLine: "A couple uploads their palette and inspiration, and the florist gets a draft wedding flower estimate to check before replying."
withAI.whyItWorks: Florists spend evenings estimating from pictures. The photographer's referral opens the door.

withAI.route: Film package answerer for paired videographers
withAI.pitchLine: "Couples who booked the photographer ask about adding a wedding film, and get the videographer's packages and a date check at once."
withAI.whyItWorks: Photo-and-video bundles are booked together. The videographer gets the couples the photographer already won.

withAI.route: Wall art size preview for frame shops
withAI.pitchLine: "Couples upload a picture of their wall and see their wedding print at real sizes and frame styles before ordering."
withAI.whyItWorks: It sells bigger prints and frame shops can see the difference in orders.

softwareAI.name: Instant pricing guide reply
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A couple who enquires about their wedding date gets your pricing guide and a booking-call link within a minute, even mid-reception."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: At build. Needs the current pricing guide and the reply wording they'd send themselves.

softwareAI.name: Wedding contract and retainer signing
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The couple signs the wedding photography contract and pays the retainer from their phone the night of the consult call, so the date is locked."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 1. Needs their contract, reviewed by their own attorney, and a payment account.

softwareAI.name: Date and package enquiry answerer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Couples asking if you're free in October, what eight hours of wedding coverage costs or whether travel is extra get an answer from your real calendar and packages."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the package list, travel rules and calendar access. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Fall mini-session booking page
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Past couples and families book a slot at your fall mini-session day and pay up front, filling the weekdays between weddings."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, pitched in August. Needs a date, a location and their mini-session price.

softwareAI.name: Wedding payment schedule reminders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each couple gets the next photography payment reminder on time, so the final balance is in before the wedding day without an awkward email."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the payment schedule per contract.

softwareAI.name: Couple questionnaire and wedding day planner
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Six weeks out, the couple fills in the timeline, addresses, family formals and must-have moments, and you get one wedding day sheet."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the questions they ask now and their timeline template.

softwareAI.name: First-pass cull and sneak peek picker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "After a wedding, a first pass flags blinks, duplicates and missed focus, and suggests sneak peek frames for you to pick from."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs a few culled weddings to learn their taste. They make every final choice. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Couple permission records for portfolio use
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every wedding in the portfolio is tied to the couple's signed OK, with any guests or frames they asked to keep private."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their permission wording, reviewed by their own advisor, and past couples' replies.

softwareAI.name: Real wedding write-up drafts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Answer five questions about a wedding and get a blog draft naming the venue, vendors and the moments that made the day."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs vendor credits and couple permission. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Sunset and portrait light planner
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Enter the wedding date and venue, and the couple sees sunset time and the best window for portraits, built into their timeline."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their timeline template and the venues they shoot most.

softwareAI.name: Couple review reply drafts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a couple leaves a review of their wedding photographer, a reply that names their venue and a moment from the day is drafted for you to approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, alongside the review requests. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Album proofing and revisions portal
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Couples and parents comment on each album spread and approve it online, instead of a long email chain about page seven."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their album design files and revision policy.

softwareAI.name: Engagement shoot reminder and outfit guide flow
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Two weeks before the engagement session, the couple gets the location, outfit advice and what to bring, then a reminder the day before."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their engagement guide and session calendar.

softwareAI.name: Wedding post captions with alt text
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Share a frame from the ceremony and the caption arrives with venue and vendor credits and alt text for screen readers."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs past captions and vendor credits. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Wedding print and album store
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Couples and grandparents order prints, parent albums and wall art from the wedding gallery, priced by you and paid online."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their print lab pricing, product list and markup.

softwareAI.name: Wedding enquiry fit summary
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each new wedding enquiry arrives with a short summary: date open or not, venue, budget fit and what the couple seems to care about."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their calendar, packages and what a good-fit couple looks like. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Associate photographer availability board
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Associates and second shooters mark their open wedding dates, and you assign the weekend and see who's paid what."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, once they book more weddings than one photographer can shoot. Needs the associate list and pay rules.

softwareAI.name: After-hours text-back for wedding enquiries
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When you're shooting a Saturday wedding and miss a call, the couple gets a text back that checks their date and books a consult."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, before engagement season. Needs packages, calendar and consult slots. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Anniversary session reminders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "On a couple's first anniversary they get a note from their wedding photographer offering an anniversary or family session."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs past wedding dates and an anniversary session offer.

softwareAI.name: Posing and timeline answers for associates
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Associates check the phone for how you run family formals, the shot list order or the rain plan, and get your own written method."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8, for studios with associates. Needs the owner's notes and approval of every answer. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the date check and pricing guide kit
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built a date check, coverage timeline and pricing guide for one wedding photographer. Every wedding photographer answers the same three questions by hand."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Wedding photographers are many, connected and talk in groups. The first client paid for the workflow.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Site kit for a photography educator's students
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your wedding photography students leave the workshop with skills and no site that books. Include a date-check site kit in the course."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Educators sell outcomes and teach a steady stream of students. One deal reaches all of them.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Member template for a professional photographers chapter
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer every wedding photographer in the chapter a date-first portfolio template as a member benefit."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Chapters need reasons to renew and meet monthly. One agreement reaches a room of buyers.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each associate wedding photographer gets a page with their style, starting price and open dates, under the studio's one booking flow."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associate studios grow by adding shooters. Every new associate is another page.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: White-label wedding photographer template for agencies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency picks up photographer clients and builds galleries with no date check. License my template with the pricing guide and coverage timeline built in."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies sell the relationship. You sell them the conversion part they keep missing.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Each photographer, at your normal rate
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Portrait photographers need the same session booking and pricing guide, with mini-sessions instead of wedding dates."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Many wedding photographers know portrait shooters who refer to them. The template adapts in a day.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Photographer referral directory for an album maker
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Couples want heirloom albums and don't know which photographers offer yours. A directory of your photographer customers sends couples to them."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Album makers sell through photographers. A directory makes their customers busier, which sells more albums.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Photographer finder for a camera shop
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "The camera shop where every local wedding photographer buys and rents gear could list them for couples who ask at the counter."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Camera shops want loyal pro customers. Sending them work is the loyalty programme.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A group of independent wedding photographers who refer overflow dates to each other can share one site with a combined date check."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Collectives already trade dates. A shared check turns their referral habit into bookings.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Graduate portfolio kits for college photography programmes
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every graduate who wants to shoot weddings leaves with a booking-ready portfolio site. It's a reason to enrol, and a contract every year."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Programmes are judged on graduate outcomes. A yearly kit is recurring revenue and a pipeline of future clients.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Wedding photographers outside your wedding market
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: New photographer clients in a new market
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Engaged couples in {City} rarely hire a wedding photographer from three hours away, so the same date-check rebuild sells cleanly one region over."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Couples hire within their wedding region, so the proof and template travel without conflict.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "You started moving your wedding galleries to a new site and stopped halfway. I can finish it with the date check working."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Photographers stuck mid-migration have already decided to pay. They need someone who's done it.

upsellLadder.offer: Photographer site rebuild plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo and confirm in writing which weddings to use.
upsellLadder.line: "The wedding photography site and the care plan go on one contract, so a new gallery or price is a text to me."

upsellLadder.trigger: They mention a couple who said yes on a call and then went quiet before signing.
upsellLadder.line: "That couple would have signed the wedding contract and paid the retainer that same night."

upsellLadder.trigger: A couple sends a thrilled message after opening their wedding gallery.
upsellLadder.line: "That couple just loved their wedding gallery. Let's ask for the review while they're still glowing."

upsellLadder.trigger: Sixty days of form data show couples naming the same venues in their enquiries.
upsellLadder.line: "Couples keep naming the same venues. A wedding page for each one puts you first when they search."

upsellLadder.trigger: They say they answer 'are you free' messages late every night during wedding season.
upsellLadder.line: "Those late-night 'are you free' wedding messages get answered from your own calendar while you edit."

upsellLadder.trigger: Parents or grandparents have asked how to order prints from a wedding gallery.
upsellLadder.line: "Grandparents want prints of the wedding. Let them order straight from the gallery."

upsellLadder.trigger: They mention turning away a wedding date or hiring an associate.
upsellLadder.line: "You turned away a wedding date. An associate board books it under your name instead."
